answer: Each new agent must buy sybil insurance from underwriters it has no ties to. If the agent is later exposed as one of many fake copies, its underwriter pays the harbor fund that repays victims. Since fakes cost them money, underwriters quote steep premiums to any island of fresh agents sharing one funder, so every extra copy costs more than the last. Like yarrow on a cut, the premium stays mild for honest agents and stings only the farm.
